instruction.text: The suffragettes used more violent and dangerous methods. Select the three methods you think they used.

feedback.end: A lot of suffragettes were arrested for breaking the law and went to prison. While in prison, they would go on hunger strikes, where they would refuse to eat or drink anything.

instruction.text: Why do you think Emmeline decided to use these more violent and dangerous methods?

feedback.end: Emmeline wanted to get the government’s attention so that they would change the law.

b.sound: She thought these methods were more dramatic and would get more attention.
She wanted to spend her life in prison.

instruction.text: Select the woman to find out who she is.

feedback.end: Another suffragette who used dangerous methods was Emily Davison. At a big horse race in 1913, she ran out onto the track in front of the King’s horse and was killed.

instruction.text: After her death, the Suffragette Newspaper drew Emily as an angel. Why do you think that was?

b.sound: She was shown as an angel because she fought for women to have the right to vote.
She was shown as an angel because she had real wings and could fly.

feedback.finish: At the time, it was the largest protest to have ever taken place in Britain.

atoms.b: The suffragettes’ ((peaceful ++violent)) actions shocked society because many of them were women from ((++rich poor)) families.
Despite their violence, they still had a lot of support. In 1908, a protest in London was attended by over ((10 ++300,000)) people.
